- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.10) — model tends to overshoot in bullish periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (especially < -0.30) — model fails to capture downside risk.
- Lagged corrections: if recent sentiment turns negative, model often holds high forecasts for 2–3 days before adjusting.
- Overshoot after spikes: model frequently peaks too high after a sharp price rise, then drops sharply — apply downward correction by 5–10% of peak value.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and ignores long-term trend — reduce forecast by 1–3% for each 3-day period of rising prices.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early summer (June) — adjust downward by 1–2% for June forecasts unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- Sentiment-weighted smoothing: if sentiment is volatile (±0.20 or more), reduce forecast volatility by 20–30% to avoid overfitting to noise.
